description:
Match request shapes to what Resend accepts. Audiences became Segments and the spec marks `audience_id` deprecated; it is removed from createBroadcast, updateBroadcast, createContact and createSegment, where `segment_id` replaces it. updateContactTopics takes the topic list as the bare JSON body, as resend-node sends it (the spec's `{ topics: [...] }` is refused with 422). updateEmail takes `scheduled_at` in the body; the spec declares no body, so the SDK could not reschedule. createEmailBatch takes the `x-batch-validation` header (`strict`, the default, or `permissive`).

Contact properties can be booleans. The spec lists only `string` and `number` for createContactProperty's `type` and types `fallback_value` as a string or number, but Resend accepts `boolean`: a request with `type: "date"` was refused with 422 "The `type` field must be one of \"string\", \"number\", or \"boolean\"." (live, 2026-10-29). A fallback value must match the property's type, so `fallback_value` also takes a boolean on createContactProperty and updateContactProperty and comes back as one from getContactProperty and listContactProperties.

A custom event's `schema` is a flat map from payload key to type, one of `string`, `number`, `boolean` or `date`. The spec says so in prose but types `schema` as an untyped document on createEvent, updateEvent, getEvent and listEvents. resend-node (`src/events/interfaces/event.ts`, `EventSchemaMap = Record<string, EventSchemaType>`) and Resend's custom events docs give the same four types. All four now target EventSchemaMap; nullability is unchanged.

An email's custom `headers` are a map from header name to string value. The spec types `headers` as an untyped document on createEmail and on each createEmailBatch item. resend-node (`src/emails/interfaces/create-email-options.interface.ts`) sends `headers?: Record<string, string>`, as the inbox send operations in this spec already type theirs. Both now target EmailHeadersMap.

traits.smithy.api#documentation: When to send the email instead: ISO 8601, or natural language such as `in 1 hour`.
`strict` (the default) rejects the whole batch when any email is invalid; `permissive` sends the valid ones and lists the rest in `errors`.
The type of a key in a custom event's payload.
A flat map from payload key to its type.
Custom headers to add to the email, from header name to value.
